## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-*juan* late-Míng synoptic commentary on the Lotus Sūtra by [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) Hānshān Déqīng 憨山德清 (1546–1623), one of the *Míngmò sìdà gāosēng* 明末四大高僧 ("four great monks of the late Míng," with [祩宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A5%A9%E5%AE%8F) Yúnqī Zhūhóng, [達觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E8%A7%80) Zǐbǎi Dáguān, and [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) Ǒuyì Zhìxù). The genre — *jījié* 擊節 ("beating-time" / "striking the rhythm") — is drawn from the classical Chinese musical metaphor of marking time at the climactic moments of a performance, and indicates a commentary that focuses on the most striking and rhetorically forceful passages of the sūtra rather than providing continuous exposition.

**Abstract**

The *Jījié* belongs to Hānshān Déqīng's substantial Mahāyāna sūtra commentarial corpus, which also includes major commentaries on the *Avataṃsaka*, the *Lèngyán*, the *Yuánjué*, the *Vimalakīrti*, and the *Awakening of Faith*. Déqīng's distinctive method combines (1) Chán-experiential reading of the sūtra-text; (2) integration of Yogācāra and Tathāgatagarbha doctrinal frameworks; and (3) sustained philological attention to the Sanskrit-Chinese translation issues. The *jījié* genre — focusing on selected striking passages — allows Déqīng to demonstrate his interpretive method on the central nodes of the Lotus's doctrinal structure without requiring the comprehensive coverage of the longer *Tōngyì*.

The work is consequently of substantial value as a witness to Déqīng's mature reading of the Lotus and as one of the principal late-Wànlì Lotus Sūtra commentaries by a major monastic figure. Together with Zhìxù's *Lúnguàn* ([KR6d0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0081)) and *Huìyì* ([KR6d0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0082)), Déqīng's *Jījié* and *Tōngyì* represent the principal late-Míng monastic Lotus Sūtra exegesis.

The dating is bracketed within Déqīng's productive period c. 1590–1623, with the work most plausibly placed in his mature exile period in Léizhōu 雷州 (Guangdong, after his exile in 1595) or in his late period at Cáoxī 曹溪.
